turn_tv_on.title: Turn this TV on for popups?
turn_tv_on.description:
Home Assistant can turn {name} on when a popup comes in and back off afterwards. To do that it needs the TV's Android TV Remote in Home Assistant.

{found}

**To pair the Android TV Remote** (one time, about a minute):
1. Open [Add Android TV Remote]({pair_remote_url}) in a new tab (or Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > Android TV Remote).
2. Enter this TV's IP address: {host}.
3. Type the code that appears on the TV.
4. Come back here and pick the new remote entity below.

On the TV, also turn on any quick start, network standby or wake on network setting so it can be woken over the network. You can change all of this later on the TV's Configure page, including turning it on only during set hours.

init.title: TV settings
init.description: Everything for this TV on one page. The sections for door buttons and popup look are shared by all your TVs. Tick "Send a test popup" at the bottom to try your settings as soon as you save.

data.send_test_popup: Send a test popup to this TV after saving

data_description.send_test_popup: Right after you save, your doorbell camera pops up with its door button, just like a real ring (the TV is turned on if your turn-on setting allows it). The button is only a test: pressing it shows a notification in Home Assistant and never unlocks or opens anything. Do not disturb is ignored for the test. Without a door-button camera, a short test video is shown.

turn_tv_on.name: Turning this TV on
turn_tv_on.description: Home Assistant can switch this TV on when a popup comes in and back off once the popup is gone. This needs an entity that powers the TV, such as its Android TV Remote entity.

data.wake_tv: Turn the TV on for popups

data.still_use_event_image: Use the camera's own event picture when it has one

data_description.power_entity: A media player or remote that switches this TV on and off. Leave empty to never turn the TV on.
data_description.wake_tv: Never: popups only show if the TV is already on. Always: turn it on any time. On a schedule: only between the two times below.
data_description.wake_tv_start: Used when "On a schedule" is chosen. If the end is earlier than the start, the window runs past midnight.
data_description.wake_tv_end: Used when "On a schedule" is chosen.
data_description.woken_tv_view: Some TVs take a while after turning on before live video shows. A still grabbed right away shows who was at the door the moment the popup was triggered. Only used when this TV was off and Home Assistant turned it on.
data_description.still_zoom: 1× shows the whole picture. Zoom in to make a face easier to see; the live video is never zoomed.
data_description.still_focus: The part of the picture to zoom into. On most doorbells, faces are in the top middle.
data_description.still_fisheye_cameras: Cameras with a round, fisheye picture (common on doorbells). Their still is flattened into a normal picture; zoom and aim then choose which part of the scene to show. Tick "Send a test popup" to see the result on this TV.
data_description.still_use_event_image: Some cameras (Eufy, for example) save their own picture of each event, often centred on the person. When it was updated around the time of the popup, it's shown as-is instead of the still below, without zoom or flattening. Otherwise the normal still is used.

do_not_disturb_settings.name: Do not disturb
do_not_disturb_settings.description: While do not disturb is on, popups to this TV are skipped (automations can still get through with ignore_do_not_disturb: true). It's on when the switch below is on, when the control entity is in the state you choose, or during the scheduled hours.

camera_buttons.name: Door buttons (all TVs)
camera_buttons.description: Pair a camera with the lock, garage door, script, or button it should control. Whenever that camera pops up on a TV, the popup gets one button for it: locks unlock, covers open, and scripts or buttons run. The popup takes remote focus, and the button needs two presses. These pairings are shared by all your TVs. Leave a row empty to remove it. Tip: point the button at a script if you want extra safety checks before it runs.

appearance.name: Popups, buttons and updates (all TVs)
appearance.description:
Settings shared by every TV. Changes apply to the next popup; no app update needed. Automations can still set popup text or duration per popup.

Popup duration applies unless an automation or the TV's own default duration sets one. Width and height of 0 use the built-in size (640 × 360). Button defaults match Home Assistant's dashboard tiles. Pausing works with most streaming apps (they pause and resume); some live-TV apps may ignore it.
